label: Friday, October 30, 2026 · AI-payoff doubt day edition
intro: Good morning. It's Friday, October 30th. Here's your Read Daily brief.

items.title: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq slip as Alphabet stock sinks 12% and AI jitters return
items.take: The three-day winning run ended Thursday as Alphabet sank 12%, its worst post-earnings reaction on record, on the capex-versus-cash-flow worry. DoorDash made the Instacart deal official: about $17 billion, $65 a share, 75% cash, with the board approving unanimously.

items.title: Stock Market News for Oct 30, 2026
items.take: The size of the Alphabet selloff makes more sense on the numbers: adjusted EPS of $2.12 missed consensus by about 28% and fell 26% year over year. September PCE inflation ran 0.5% monthly and 3.6% yearly, in line but still hot, which keeps the pressure on.

items.title: Stock Market Today: Dow, S&P Live Updates for October 30, 2026
items.take: The AI-payoff doubt widened past Alphabet on Thursday: another batch of disappointing tech earnings deepened the selloff, the Nasdaq 100 fell about 3%, and Intel sank 29% after its revenue forecast missed estimates.

items.title: S&P 500 sinks as Amazon, Intel losses shake Wall Street
items.take: Friday opens with the selloff still running on weak Amazon and Intel results, rekindling concern about the payoff from massive AI spending. One pocket of green: Exxon and Chevron rose premarket after both beat, helped by soaring refining margins.

items.title: Amodei called for an AI slowdown, then informed investors he’d race ahead
items.take: Anthropic publicly backed an AI slowdown, then told IPO investors it would race ahead, and the Post lays out the gap in black and white. It is a sharp lens on the week’s theme: the same firms selling caution to the public are selling growth to markets.

items.title: What’s News: ‘AI Mode’ Is Denting Google’s Search Revenue
items.take: Today’s rotation pick lands squarely on theme: WSJ’s What’s News digs into AI Mode eating into Google’s search revenue, the very business underwriting Alphabet’s AI spending spree. Good context for a rough earnings morning.
